title: WhatsApp Starts Charging for Customer Service Replies on 1 October
desc: From 1 October Meta charges for service messages and for utility replies inside the 24 hour window. The free tier is 1,000 a month and does not roll over.
keywords: whatsapp service message pricing, whatsapp business api pricing 2026, whatsapp customer service window charges, meta business agent pricing, whatsapp free tier 1000 messages
cta: Want your client messaging repriced before 1 October?
body:
September 21, 2026. If you or your clients answer customers on WhatsApp, the replies have been free since November 2024. In ten days they are not. Meta's WhatsApp Business Platform pricing page, updated on 10 September 2026, sets out a set of changes effective 1 October 2026, and two of them turn message types that currently cost nothing into billable ones.

What changes on 1 October

  1. Service messages become chargeable, at the same rates Meta already charges for utility and authentication in each market.
  2. Utility messages sent in response to users, inside an open 24 hour customer service window, become chargeable. Those have been free since 1 July 2025.
  3. A new free tier arrives: 1,000 delivered service messages per month, per business phone number.
  4. Marketing rates rise in Kuwait, Mexico, Morocco, Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Rest of Middle East and Rest of Asia Pacific. Utility and authentication rates rise in Kazakhstan, Kuwait, Morocco, Oman, Pakistan, Peru, South Africa and Ukraine, and fall in Bangladesh, Iraq, Nepal and Sri Lanka.
  5. Nine markets move out of their regional pricing buckets to stand alone on the rate cards, each with a new authentication international rate, announced on 27 May 2026.

Meta's own history section makes the shape of this clear. Service conversations became free for all businesses on 1 November 2024. The free period lasted almost exactly two years.

The free tier is 1,000 and it does not roll over

The detail that decides whether 1,000 is generous or irrelevant is how it is consumed. Meta states that each business phone number has one shared free tier covering both one to one and group service deliveries. A one to one delivery consumes one unit. A group send consumes one unit per delivered recipient. So a single broadcast to 500 people spends half the month's allowance in one action.

Unused messages do not roll over, and the tier resets monthly per phone number: 1,000 for October with no roll over, 1,000 for November with no roll over. Service messages also sit outside the volume tier system, which Meta scopes to utility and authentication only, so there is no discount for sending more.

No payment method means messages stop

The sharpest line on the page is easy to skim past. If there is no payment method on the WhatsApp Business account, Meta will deliver service messages within the free tier but will not deliver them once the free tier is used.

That is a delivery stop, not an invoice. A small business on a free tier with no card on file will simply stop being able to answer its own customers partway through a busy month, and the failure will look like a bug rather than a billing setting.

Your billing dashboard will read the old field

Meta is changing the values inside the status webhook, not just the rate card. Through 30 September, a service message or an in window utility reply arrives with pricing type free_customer_service and billable false. As of 1 October, once the free tier is used, the same message arrives with type regular and billable true.

Any dashboard, spreadsheet or automation that counts spend by matching on free_customer_service will keep reporting those messages as free, because the field it keys on no longer appears. The fix is to trust the billable boolean and the category, not the type string.

One more practical warning comes from Meta itself: the USD PDF of the new rates contained errors in the volume tiers for specific markets and was corrected on 14 September 2026. Meta asks customers to rely on the CSVs published since 1 September or the PDF republished on 14 September. If you priced a client's October messaging off that PDF in early September, reprice it.

What it means for operators

Agencies running client inboxes should do four things this week. Pull last month's service and in window utility volumes per phone number and compare them against 1,000, because that number is now a budget. Confirm a payment method exists on every WhatsApp Business account you manage, including the small ones nobody has touched since setup. Re-point any billing automation at the billable field. And check whether any of your clients bill in AED or MXN, because both of those markets take a marketing rate rise on the same day.

The structural point is that the cheap part of WhatsApp was the conversation after the customer replied, which is exactly the part an AI agent is good at holding. Once every reply has a price, the metric that matters stops being messages sent and becomes cost per resolved conversation. That is a routing and deflection problem before it is a copy problem, and it is the same arithmetic we run when we build client messaging on white label GoHighLevel or wire it into an existing stack with AI automation.
faqs: What exactly becomes chargeable on WhatsApp on 1 October 2026?

Two things. Service messages, which are the free form replies you can send inside an open 24 hour customer service window, and utility template messages sent in response to users inside that same window. Both are free today. From 1 October they are billed at the same per market rates as utility and authentication.
How does the 1,000 message free tier work?

Each business phone number gets one shared free tier of 1,000 delivered service messages a month, covering both one to one and group sends. A one to one delivery uses one unit and a group send uses one unit per delivered recipient. It resets monthly and unused messages do not roll over.
What happens if there is no payment method on the account?

Meta will deliver service messages inside the free tier and will not deliver them after the free tier is used. It is a hard stop on delivery rather than a bill, so any account you manage without a card on file can go silent mid month.
Will our WhatsApp spend reporting break?

It can. The pricing type in the status webhook changes from free_customer_service to regular for these messages once the free tier is used, and billable changes from false to true. Any report that filters on the free_customer_service string will under count spend from 1 October. Key on the billable field instead.
